experiment: HLS external learning-mechanism comparison: MIS-v2 vs Nembhard Direct

ontology.A_scenario: 3 agents × 3 task types; C5 demand; one unit of current-task work per period; same paired task path and resource catalog.
ontology.B_mechanisms: MIS-v2 evolves bounded competence; Nembhard Direct evolves cumulative task-specific experience and evaluates the published direct productivity curve. Nembhard indirect-transfer component is excluded.
ontology.C_organizations: same LinUCB-disjoint, fixed specialist map and current-output reactive selector under both mechanisms.
ontology.policy_learning_vs_agent_learning: LinUCB updates its arm-specific selection model; the mechanism updates only the agent-task physical state. These states are logged separately.

Nembhard_parameters.calibration: k=1,r=1,p=C0/(1-C0), hence Eq.(1) gives P(D=0)=C0 cellwise; p is an equivalent-prior-exposure calibration, not an empirical Nembhard parameter estimate.

configuration.reward: deterministic normalized effective output per assigned unit: MIS competence C[i,k] or Nembhard P[i,k](D), both in [0,1]; initial expected output matrices are exactly matched.
configuration.resources: one selected agent, effort=1, shared budget=1, individual limit=1, period duration=1; no separate development cost
configuration.action_catalog: for task k, exactly three actions, one unit assigned to a single agent on k; same catalog for all methods and mechanisms
configuration.fixed_policy: task_i maps to agent_i; predeclared from the diagonal initial specialization, no evaluation outcomes used
configuration.reactive_policy: current-period P0 functional-effort ranking; MIS uses existing P0ProductionOnlyNK, Nembhard uses existing NembhardOracleRouterNK with the same one-agent catalog and current true productivity; no lookahead
configuration.LinUCB: unmodified disjoint implementation; 6 features (task one-hot plus current productivity of all agents for that task), alpha from Li et al. Eq.(4) with delta=0.05; only selected reward observed
configuration.information: task and current true task-specific competence/productivity are observable to all; no future demand; no unselected reward; Nembhard k,p,r and D are known in this synthetic validation
configuration.transfer: disabled / absent in both compared transitions; no cross-task or cross-agent state update
configuration.Nembhard_fidelity_boundary: Eq.(1) direct-experience curve and HLS D+=effort×duration convention only; not a full reproduction of Nembhard & Bentefouet (2015).

limitations: The Nembhard source's indirect-transfer model is not integrated; prior source audit records unresolved simultaneity and dimensional ambiguities in Eqs. (A-3)/(A-4).
Nembhard p values are calibrated to match the MIS initial output profile; they are not published empirical estimates.
The comparison uses normalized synthetic effective output and perfect state observation, not a practical production dataset.
C5 task sequence is stochastic and paired; rewards are deterministic conditional on state and assignment, so SD reflects demand-path variation only.
LinUCB's context/reward relation is linear by construction, but this small pilot does not claim its published regret guarantee or general superiority.
